If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testTrailingSpecial` in `QuotedPrintableCodecTest` is testing the behavior of the `QuotedPrintableCodec` class. The test sets a plain text string and an expected encoded string with a special character to test encoding. The failure indicates that the encoding does not match the expected value. The current bug report mentions that the `QuotedPrintableCodec` does not support soft line breaks as per the example on Wikipedia.

Looking at the test snippet, the plain text includes a special character `sp=` and the expected encoded string includes the representation of this special character as `sp=3D=\r\ncial chars.`. This aligns with the issue that special characters are not properly encoded in the `QuotedPrintableCodec`.

To further investigate the issue, it would be beneficial to review the implementation of the `QuotedPrintableCodec` class to see how it handles encoding special characters and soft line breaks.

I will now retrieve and inspect the code snippet for the `QuotedPrintableCodec` class to identify if there is a missing handling for special characters and soft line breaks in the encoding process.

messages.content:
The `encode` method in the `QuotedPrintableCodec` class finally encodes the input string by converting it to an ASCII String. It uses the `encode` method with `String.getBytes(charset)` to get the bytes of the string before encoding it. This method does not handle special characters or soft line breaks in a way that aligns with the expected behavior discussed in the Wikipedia example.

To address the issue where special characters are not properly encoded with soft line breaks, the `encode` method in the `QuotedPrintableCodec` class needs to be modified to handle such cases correctly. Specifically, it should encode special characters like `=` and consider soft line breaks `\r\n` during the encoding process.

The root cause of the test failure in `QuotedPrintableCodecTest` is the lack of proper handling for special characters and soft line breaks in the `QuotedPrintableCodec` class implementation.

Considering this analysis, the following method needs to be fixed:
- `org.apache.commons.codec.net.QuotedPrintableCodec.encode(java.lang.String, java.lang.String)`

This method should be updated to correctly encode special characters and handle soft line breaks according to the `quoted-printable` specification.

If you have any more questions or need further assistance, feel free to ask!
